To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) translation is not a marginal phenomenon in literary culture, (2) translation is not only an activity of the past, but a vital part of the present, (3) translation is not an activity that is confined to the margins of literature, but is an activity that is central to the production of literature, (4) translation is not the result of a process that is independent from other processes in literary culture, but is the result of a complex interaction between the various processes, and

the translation of literary works is an activity that can be described and analysed in the light of a number of theoretical models, that the translation process can be reconstructed on the basis of the available evidence, and that this process is subject to a number of constraints that have to do with the nature of literature, with the nature of translation and with the nature of society.

a) translation is not an isolated activity, but part of a complex of cultural and literary phenomena; b) the translator is not an isolated individual, but a social being who is part of a network of relationships with other translators, authors, publishers and readers; c) the translated text is not an isolated text, but part of an intertextual network of relationships with the source text, other translations and other texts in the target literature; and d) the translation process is not an isolated event
